Ava (oncall): Heads-up — after the 02:15 deploy we’re seeing a sharp 5xx spike on /v1/generate. Errors jumped ~7x at ~02:20, and currently about 18% of requests are 5xx. Canary was at 10% when I noticed.
DeployBot: Canary rollout started deploy-20260315-42 -> traffic 5% -> 10% -> 30% per policy.
Ava (oncall): Adding logs, sample 502s show gateway timeouts talking to runtime pool and auth header rejections.
Priya (sre): Confirmed. Traces show increased latency at gateway -> runtime handshake. Many errors are 502/504; some 503 with "upstream read timeout".
Diego (platform): I see a recent config flip: feature_flag.inference.canary_route was changed in feature-store at 02:14. The flag should’ve been scoped to service: inference-canary but looks like it leaked to inference-prod routes.
Marcus (eng-runtime): If the canary route header is present on prod traffic runtime picks a different routing table (new sharding). That would explain runtime OOM/retry storms.
Lin (customer-success): We’ve got 2 priority-1 escalations from customers (Acme Health, Satya Labs) complaining about consistent 5xx and timeouts for production keys. They're seeing failed requests and are asking for ETA.
Ava (oncall): Repro steps I used: curl against gateway with a normal API key + injected header X-Canary-Route: beta

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <PROD_KEY>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -H "X-Canary-Route: beta" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3","input":"hello"}'
```

That returned 502s reliably from a subset of nodes. Without the header it’s fine (mostly 200s).
Priya (sre): Good repro. That narrows it to traffic tagging. Log sample from gateway (truncated):

```
[02:19:47] request_id=abc123 host=gateway-12 route=prod -> attach_flag=beta upstream=runtime-05 error="upstream read timeout"
[02:19:48] request_id=def456 host=gateway-12 route=prod -> attach_flag=beta upstream=runtime-09 error="502 Bad Gateway: peer reset"
```

Diego (platform): How did the flag leak? The patch was supposed to gate by workspace env but I see the rollout rule uses prefix match that accidentally matched prod-hosts. I’m rolling a fix to the flag service now.
Marcus (eng-runtime): Meanwhile runtime sharding expects the beta header to carry new shard-id header X-Shard: b23. Missing shard header causes fallback to a heavy sync path that overloads the pool. We can patch runtime to be more defensive but that’s riskier mid-incident.
Ava (oncall): Immediate mitigation options? 1) Kill the flag at the feature-store (fast). 2) Rollback the deploy that introduced the routing change (deploy-20260315-42). 3) Emergency gateway rule to strip X-Canary-Route header for prod traffic. Which is fastest?
Diego (platform): Killing flag is fastest (single flip). I’ll do that and monitor. If we see no improvement in 2m, we fallback to rollback.
SupportBot: Notifying accounts team — Acme Health opened a ticket 10291, Satya Labs ticket 10292. Both flagged as P1.
Priya (sre): After flip at 02:23, error rate dipped but still above baseline — 5xx from 18% -> 9% over 3 minutes. Some nodes still showing elevated error rates. Could be in-flight traffic that retained header.
Ava (oncall): Traffic percentage graph: canary % briefly jumped to 30% at 02:17 due to mis-evaluated rollout rule. That would explain why impact increased rapidly.
Marcus (eng-runtime): Suggest draining the affected runtime instances (runtime-05, runtime-09, runtime-12) — they have high retry queues. Draining will force new connections to healthy pools. I can trigger a drain.
Diego (platform): Drains initiated. Also pushing a temporary gateway filter to DROP X-Canary-Route headers for requests with workspace=prod. Patch id: gf-20260315-9.
Ava (oncall): After drain and header strip, 5xx down to 3% in last minute but still seeing spikes tied to cached KV lookups failing (auth fallback path).
Marcus (eng-runtime): I can add a defensive guard to runtime config to short-circuit the heavy sync path if X-Shard is absent and not consume extra memory — quick binary flag change, can be live-configged in ~10min. Would reduce residual errors.
Priya (sre): Agree that safe guard is good. Diego, can you approve live config change?
Diego (platform): Approving. Marcus, go ahead. Keep it scoped to canary-route absent only.
Marcus (eng-runtime): Pushing live config now -> runtime.live:guard_missing_shard=true.
DeployBot: live-config update applied to runtime pool. change_id=lc-20260315-7
Ava (oncall): Great — residual 5xx now ~0.6%. Traces look healthy.
Lin (customer-success): Messaging plan for customers? I’ll post status: we detected a config flag leak during canary rollout that briefly routed prod traffic to canary path; we’ve reverted the flag, drained impacted nodes, and applied a defensive runtime config. Asking for permission to say ETA: "service restored, investigating" in public comms.
Diego (platform): Yes, fine to say that. Internally we need to run a postmortem: root cause is rollout rule mismatch + missing guard in runtime that made it brittle.
Priya (sre): Please capture the exact timeline and deploy IDs. I’ll keep the incident open for 3 more hours for monitoring.
Ava (oncall): Action items: Diego - submit rollback/flag gating fix PR (#4802) and coordinate staged deploy; Marcus - follow-up runtime guard permanent patch and add unit tests; Priya - incident blameless postmortem; Lin - customer messages + Credits for Acme Health and Satya Labs.
SupportBot: Tickets updated: Acme Health (10291) -> status: service restored, credit pending; Satya Labs (10292) -> status: service restored, credit pending.
Ava (oncall): Closing note: nice quick coordination. No full rollback needed but keep rollback plan ready in case of regression on metrics. :thumbsup:
Diego (platform): I’ll also add a test in rollout rules to prevent prefix matches that cross env boundaries.
Marcus (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: adding log tagging to detect canary headers on prod traffic automatically.
Priya (sre): Logging the incident and timeline now. Will ping when PM/ops review ready.
Lin (customer-success): I’ve sent customer updates and opened credit requests.
Ava (oncall): Thanks everyone. I’m going to update the incident channel with the post-incident summary in ~1h.
